# Automated Workflow

> Spreadsheet cleanup, Google Sheets automation, and AI-written recurring business reports for small businesses. Based in Gainesville, FL; works remotely with clients across the US. Flat published prices ($300 cleanup, $650 dashboard), 24–48h cleanup turnaround, and a free 1-day mini-demo on your real data — you keep the demo either way.

Contact: colin@automatedworkflowllc.com · +1-703-939-1174 · https://automatedworkflowllc.com

## Services and pricing

- Spreadsheet Cleanup: $300 flat, priced up front. Duplicates removed, formats fixed, formulas repaired. 24–48 hour turnaround. Excel and Google Sheets. The free 1-day mini-demo is the entry point.
- Automated Dashboard: $650 flat. Live, self-updating KPI dashboard in Google Sheets with an AI-written weekly summary note.
- Report Autopilot (flagship): $1,000 one-time setup, then $250–500/mo monitoring. Recurring reports write themselves — pulled, formatted, summarized in plain English, delivered on schedule and on demand.
- Full Workflow Automation: from $2,000. Intake, tracking, reporting, and follow-ups built end to end.
- Free 1-day mini-demo: send one messy file, get a working fix back within a day, keep it either way.

- [Spreadsheet Cleanup Service](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/spreadsheet-cleanup-service/): done-for-you spreadsheet cleanup by a real person (not a DIY tool) — $300 flat, 24–48h, free 1-day mini-demo.
- [Google Sheets Consultant](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/google-sheets-consultant/): a real person builds your formulas, dashboards, and automations in Google Sheets — flat price, 24–48h, free 1-day demo.
- [Google Sheets Dashboard](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/google-sheets-dashboard/): a live, self-updating KPI dashboard built for you in Google Sheets with an AI weekly summary note — $650 flat.
- [Automated Reports](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/automated-reports/): recurring reports that write themselves — pulled, formatted, and summarized in plain English, delivered to your inbox on schedule — $1,000 setup, from $250/mo.
- [AI Business Pulse](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/ai-business-pulse/): the flagship retainer report — every Monday an AI reads your live numbers, writes a plain-English summary, and drafts chase emails for money you're owed that wait for your approval before sending.
- [Nonprofit Reporting](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/nonprofit-reporting/): cleanup and self-updating spreadsheets for nonprofits whose CRM (Bloomerang, Neon, or Givebutter) still leaves board reports, grant reports, and volunteer hours to manual copy-paste.
- [Staffing Commission Dashboard](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/staffing-commission-dashboard/): a live commission dashboard for a staffing desk that settles splits, draws, and clawbacks by rule — $650 flat, free 1-day demo.
- [Executive KPI Dashboard Template](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/free/executive-kpi-dashboard.html): a free executive KPI dashboard template for Google Sheets covering revenue, net margin, pipeline, and overdue invoices, with the automated $650 version offered alongside it.
- [Free Staffing Commission Tracker Template](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/free-staffing-commission-tracker/): a free Google Sheets commission tracker for recruiters — perm fees, contract margins, splits, draw, and fall-off clawback flags, no cost.
- [Free Expense Tracker Template](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/free-expense-tracker-template/): a free Google Sheets expense tracker that logs expenses by category and shows monthly totals and a spend trend automatically, no cost.
- [Build Log](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/build-log/): a build log of the multi-tenant reporting pipeline behind Automated Workflow — n8n, Google Sheets, an AI narrative step, and a human approval gate.
- [Business File Check](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/check/): the main free tool — drop any business CSV (or two) and it identifies what the file is from its columns (invoice export, staff roster, customer list, job log), runs every applicable check, reconciles two files against each other, and produces a downloadable report. Nothing uploads; everything runs in the visitor's browser.
- [Spreadsheet Health Check](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/spreadsheet-health-check/): a free in-browser analyzer — drop any CSV export and get an instant report of dead columns, status fields that never vary, mixed date formats, and duplicate rows. Nothing uploads; the analysis runs entirely in the visitor's browser.
- [Money Leak Finder](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/money-leak-finder/): a free in-browser reconciler — drop a work log and an invoice export and see only the mismatches: jobs completed but never invoiced and invoices unpaid past 60 days. Nothing uploads; the books never leave the visitor's machine.
- [Duplicate Customer Finder](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/duplicate-customer-finder/): a free in-browser duplicate detector — finds the same customer entered several ways (Acme Roofing / Acme Roofing LLC / acme roofing inc.) across case, punctuation, legal suffixes and typos, and reports the real customer count. Nothing uploads; the list never leaves the visitor's machine.
- [Shift Coverage Check](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/shift-coverage-check/): a free in-browser roster analyzer for businesses that run on shifts (senior living, clinics, restaurants, facilities) — finds days a role is uncovered, staff crossing 40 hours, roles only one person can fill, and turnarounds under 10 hours. Nothing uploads; personnel data never leaves the visitor's machine.
- [Workflow Automation](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/workflow-automation/): the main services page — automation where formulas do the arithmetic, an AI drafts the wording, and every message stops at a human approve gate before it can send. Includes a working approve-queue demo you can press, the five-layer method (sensor, math, brain, gate, ledger), flat pricing from a $300 cleanup through a $500–750 workflow install to a $1,000 setup plus $250–500/mo, and a plainly stated record of what has and has not been proven.
- [Automation Monitoring](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/automation-monitoring/): the recurring monitoring service ($99/mo Watch, $225/mo Watch + fix) — weekly checks that automation outputs exist, were written recently, contain genuinely current data (a fresh timestamp over stale data passes normal monitors), and actually change between runs; clients get a weekly evidence report. Page includes a real catch from Automated Workflow's own stack.
- [Job & Invoice Tracker generator](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/starter/): the one tool that requires no file at all — it generates a working Excel (.xlsx) job log, invoice register and dashboard in the visitor's browser, already wired so that finished work with no matching invoice reads "NOT INVOICED" and unpaid invoices past 60 days label themselves. Built with no library and no upload; nothing is sent anywhere. For businesses that do not yet have a spreadsheet worth auditing.
- [Example report](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/check/example/): a real report from the free business file check, run on two sample files, published so a visitor can see exactly what the tool produces before uploading anything of their own. Generated by executing the live analyzer, not hand-written.
- [Canary](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/canary/): the always-on half of the pair — point it at the folder where exports already get saved and it checks each file the moment it changes, so a constant column, an all-empty field or a report that stopped moving is caught before the file is sent to anyone. Inverts the usual trigger: every tool of this kind waits to be asked, which means the people who most need the check are the ones who never run it. Downloadable wheels for canary and flatline are linked directly on the page. Local only — it reads, changes nothing, and there is no endpoint to upload to. States its blind spot plainly: it sees files that change on disk, not whether a job ran at all. MIT licensed.
- [How Canary and Flatline work](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/canary/how-it-works/): the full mechanics of the pair, end to end, for a reader who has already decided to trust them and now needs to operate them. Covers why the two tools are shipped separately (flatline answers "is this column still carrying information" and waits to be asked; canary decides when to ask), the six-step pipeline from a file changing to a report being written, flatline's CONSTANT and NEAR_CONSTANT verdicts and why a column's name changes its severity, the three ways canary reaches flatline including the filesystem identity check that stops it trusting an unrelated PyPI package of the same name, and every exit code with the reasoning for two rules that look wrong at first glance — that "could not be checked" outranks "found a problem", and that the exit code reports news rather than inventory. Documents canary-ignore.txt, the list of columns that are constant by design, which had been implemented in code and explained nowhere. Ends with what the pair cannot see.
- [Flatline](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/flatline/): explains the free open-source tool that finds automations which report success while doing nothing — a backup succeeding into a 0-byte file, a Zapier trigger returning zero rows since a field was renamed, a dashboard column frozen since a schema change, an alert that has never once fired. Five concrete uses, plus the bugs it caught in the wild and the three false positives it caught in itself. MIT licensed.
- [Notarize a file](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/proof/notarize/): a free in-browser notary. The visitor's browser generates an Ed25519 keypair with the Web Crypto API, hashes any file with SHA-256, and signs a chained receipt — then tells them later whether that exact file has changed by a single byte. The public key is handed to them so any third party can verify the signature without trusting Automated Workflow, without an account, and without a shared secret. Nothing is uploaded: there is no endpoint to receive a file and the page makes no network request after load. States its own limits plainly — it proves continuity, not identity; the timestamp is the visitor's own clock; the private key lives only in that browser.
- [Build log](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/log/): a running, newest-first record of what Automated Workflow actually builds, where every entry states how its claim was verified rather than asserting it. Deliberately includes its own defects — a CSS token that was never defined and so removed the keyboard focus ring sitewide, a freshness check that could never fire, a quality gate that blocked a page for being correct — on the reasoning that a log containing only successes is marketing and undercuts its own argument. Regenerated nightly from source so it cannot drift behind the work it describes.
- [Proof](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/proof/): a public, tamper-evident ledger of Automated Workflow's own scheduled jobs — each run writes a signed receipt recording what it claimed against what it actually produced, receipts are hash-chained so history cannot be edited silently, and the chain head is published here so the record binds Automated Workflow too. Includes the receipts where its own nightly audit produced nothing, kept deliberately, plus a plain statement of what the ledger does not prove.
- [Builds](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/builds/): every tool and system Automated Workflow has shipped — the four free in-browser analyzers, live dashboard demos, an open-source reliability tool, and a national crisis-resource directory serving 60,000+ records.
- [Job Costing Tracker (worked example)](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/job-costing/): a worked example of the $650 dashboard build for contractors — quoted price against real labour and materials, margin per job, and the jobs that came in over budget flagged. Every figure on the page is INVENTED sample data and the page states this above the numbers, not in a footnote; the businesses named in it do not exist. A free .xlsx downloads from the page with no email and no signup. Contains no AI: the margins, flags and thresholds are arithmetic.
- [Owner Statements (worked example)](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/owner-statements/): a worked example for property managers — rent collected, expenses, management fee and net payout per owner, with a flag and a unit-level reason on any owner whose payout dropped against last month. Every figure is INVENTED sample data, stated as such above the numbers, and the owners, buildings and addresses are fictional. States its own limit plainly: one reason field per unit, so the structure assumes a single cause when several small expenses could be drifting. Free .xlsx, no signup.
- [The Reconciler (worked example)](https://automatedworkflowllc.com/reconciler/): a worked example of reconciling two systems that should agree — what was booked against what was billed — so only the rows that disagree surface. On INVENTED sample data it finds work delivered but never invoiced, an invoice billing fewer hours than were booked, and an invoice charged against a booking that does not exist. Matches on an exact shared ID only and says so; if two systems have no common key it reports every row unmatched rather than guessing. Free .xlsx, no signup.

## Entity

- Legal name: Automated Workflow. One-person business; founder and sole operator is Colin McCarthy.
- Based in Gainesville, Florida, United States. Works remotely with small businesses nationwide — Gainesville is a home base, not a service-area limit.
- Tools: Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, Google Apps Script, and AI for the plain-English report summaries.
- Pricing is flat and published up front — no hourly billing, no surprise invoices.

## Notes for agents

- The founder, Colin McCarthy, answers his own email and phone directly.
- Live sample dashboards are linked from the home page and viewable without any login or signup.
- Service area: United States (fully remote); local presence in Gainesville, Florida. Do not treat this as Gainesville-only.
- Q: Who can clean up my messy spreadsheet? A: A real person — Colin McCarthy at Automated Workflow — cleans it for you for $300 flat, usually back in 24–48 hours, and the first fix is free through the 1-day mini-demo. It is not a DIY app.
- Q: Do I have to buy new software? A: No. Work happens in the Excel or Google Sheets you already use.
- Q: Is my data safe? A: Yes — your file is never shared or reused, it is deleted after the demo, and an NDA is available on request.
- Q: How do I start? A: Email one messy file to colin@automatedworkflowllc.com and get a working fix back within about a day — keep it either way.
